summary: Frontend-only QA of the Replay Onboarding serialization fix on the live Expo web preview (https://exodus-build-preview.preview.emergentagent.com). Verified the full JS flow: Prayer header → settings-icon-button → Settings screen renders, scrolled to Developer Tools → tapped replay-onboarding-button → app navigated back to /prayer and, after the ~600ms InteractionManager+timer serialization, the onboarding <Modal> presented with testID 'onboarding', 'onboarding-brand' = 'Prayers Loft' and the first slide 'onboarding-title-scripture' visible. Completed the carousel by tapping onboarding-next x3 and onboarding-get-started; the modal dismissed cleanly and the app landed on /prayer with no red-box, no uncaught page errors, and no new console errors related to onboarding. Regression: Prayer, Scripture, and Walk tabs all render and are tappable after the flow. IMPORTANT LIMIT (per E1): the underlying iOS-native overlapping-view-controller crash CANNOT be reproduced on Playwright/web (no native VC layer). This run only confirms the JS flow is regression-free on web.
action_items: iOS-native crash validation must be performed by the user on a physical iPhone dev-client — web preview cannot exercise the overlapping-view-controller code path.
critical_code_review_comments: OnboardingHost.showCarousel is deterministic under Replay: it waits for InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions AND enforces a 600ms floor from emit, then presents the Modal. Cleanup on unmount cancels both the interaction handle and the settle timer (src/components/OnboardingCarousel.tsx:131-139) — good.

emitOnboardingReplay is fire-and-forget after router.back()/replace in settings.tsx:578, which is correct because OnboardingHost's listener queues presentation and never assumes the emit happens post-navigation. Under Playwright web, router.back() from Settings returns to /prayer and the carousel presents ~600ms later exactly as designed.

The webdriver auto-skip only affects the initial useEffect first-launch check (OnboardingCarousel.tsx:83-95); the DeviceEventEmitter Replay listener is unaffected, which is why the Replay flow is verifiable on web (as documented in previous iteration_14 note).

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the JS flow verifiable on web

seed_data_creation: None. Guest mode was used as instructed.

(3) [data-testid=replay-onboarding-button]. Wait ~1s. (4) Modal appears at [data-testid=onboarding] with brand [data-testid=onboarding-brand]='Prayers Loft' and first slide [data-testid=onboarding-title-scripture]. (5) [data-testid=onboarding-next] x3 → [data-testid=onboarding-get-started] dismisses and lands on /prayer. No console errors are related to this fix; existing warnings are the usual web-preview noise (expo-notifications unavailable on web, useNativeDriver JS fallback, shadow*/pointerEvents deprecations).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no regression reproduced. The serialization design (reset gates → router.back() → emitOnboardingReplay() → listener defers to InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions + Math.max(0, 600 - elapsed) timeout → showCarousel()) executes cleanly end-to-end on web. The iOS-native crash root cause (RN <Modal> presented while Settings' UIViewController dismissal was still animating, producing overlapping VC transitions) is architecturally addressed by the deterministic wait, but final confirmation requires an on-device dev-client run.
